title: Thadrak Kanjur 'Bum Ca
shelf_note: A manuscript Kanjur volume of the Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā ('Bum), handwritten pothi leaves. It belongs on the Tibetan shelf.
structure_note: Each photograph holds two pothi leaves (I5), and the run is not in reading order. Text runs 524-top → 524-bottom → 525-top (ending 'དེ་ནས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས།') → 526-top ('ལྷའི་དབང་པོ་བརྒྱ་བྱིན་ལ་བཀའ་སྩལ་པ', ending '…ཐོབ་པར') → 525-bottom ('གྱུར་པ་དང་།…') → 526-bottom. The bottom leaf of 525 and the top leaf of 526 are swapped in reading order, so a reader hits a non sequitur at 525. The run has no printed numbers, and 439 of 556 pages are translated.

tr_errors.problem: misparsed: dharmas were taught BY WHICH beings enter; the English makes the entering the content of the teachings

book_verdict: The BDRC OCR is serviceable and the translation is faithful to the stock formulas. The defect is structural: two leaves per photograph, with leaves swapped between consecutive records, so the reading order breaks at page 525.

title: Tantrik Texts Vol. VI (1917)
shelf_note: The Kālīvilāsa Tantra (Avalon ed.); Sanskrit tantra shelf. The title should name the work.
structure_note: Printed page numbers are sparse. Record 23's OCR takes the signature mark '२' at the foot as page-num '2', which explains the 16 backsteps and 22 repeats. They are misreads, not a splice.

tr_errors.problem: translates the reconstruction and borrows 'never' from v.13

ocr_errors.problem: signature recorded as the page number

tr_errors.english: (absent)

book_verdict: Ritual verse, mostly rendered faithfully. But the OCR on page 21 normalises वैश्यभावत्वं to वैष्णवत्वं, so the English says a Śūdra becomes a Vaiṣṇava, not a Vaiśya. The scan is low resolution and some half-lines are reconstructed.

title: Opus mago-cabbalisticum et theosophicum
shelf_note: Welling's Opus mago-cabbalisticum (1784), section on Sulphur; esoteric/kabbalah shelf.
structure_note: Record 242 is a second copy of printed page 180 (identical to 240) placed after page 181 (241): a duplicate record (I2), translated twice. There are 801 records against pages_count 794 and 127 printed repeats, so the duplication is likely widespread, not a misread numeral.

title: Sefer ha-Zohar (Cremona 1558)
